data.description:
WHERE: toolbench/report.py:103-134 (_sampling_notes), tally_skips in toolbench/reducer.py.

WHAT: when the sampling spread crosses SPREAD_THRESHOLD, the warning names its two possible causes -- (1) --limit truncating the corpus unevenly across agents, and (2) skip attrition -- but it cannot say WHICH, or in what proportion, whenever both are live.

It resolves only the degenerate case. With zero skips it can rule attrition out and state --limit as fact (report.py:111-121). With skips non-empty (report.py:122-134) it falls back to hedging: the spread may come from --limit truncation, from attrition, or from both -- re-running without --limit is not guaranteed to fix it.

ROOT CAUSE: the shape of the tally, not the wording. tally_skips reduces a list[SkipRecord] into dict[SkipReason, int] -- agent identity is destroyed at aggregation time. So even though we know 40 sessions were skipped, we cannot say that 38 of them were agent X, which is the fact that would let the note apportion the spread.

FIX SKETCH: key the tally by (agent, reason) rather than reason alone -- SkipRecord would need to carry the agent, which means the discovery path must stamp it on the ref before the skip is recorded. Then the note can say something load-bearing: agent X lost 38 of its 40 candidate sessions to attrition, which accounts for the spread; --limit is not the cause. The Skipped by reason tally can keep rendering its current collapsed view.

NOT A REWORDING: no phrasing of the existing note can recover the missing dimension. This ticket is upstream data-model work.
data.title: Uneven-sampling warning cannot apportion between its two causes: the skip tally is keyed by reason, not by agent

provenance.reason: TB-33 review follow-up: named limitation in the uneven-sampling disclosure

data.note: TB-33 review follow-up: surfaced while reviewing the agent-sampling disclosure work

data.body:
Scope widened: two open roborev reviews on `fix/tb-33-agent-sampling-disclosure` are blocked on this ticket's data-model fix and were deferred into it rather than fixed separately.

**roborev job #95 (commit ebbb6e5) — CONFIRMED live at branch HEAD.** The no-skip branch of `_sampling_notes` (toolbench/report.py:111-121) asserts `--limit` as the definite cause of an uneven spread. But `--limit` defaults to `None` (passive.py:217), truncates only `if args.limit is not None` (passive.py:269), and `render_report` takes no `limit` parameter at all (report.py:238-253). So a `--all` run with zero skips and an uneven spread tells the user to "re-run without `--limit`" — a flag they never passed. False cause and false remedy. Accepted fix shape: thread an explicit limit-applied/truncated signal into `render_report` / `_sampling_notes`, and soften the zero-skip wording when no limit was confirmed.

**roborev job #66, finding 2 (MEDIUM) — also live.** `_sampling_notes` derives `unreached` from `reducer.agents[a].sessions == 0` (report.py:91-101), which cannot distinguish "the window never looked at this agent" from "we looked, and every one of its sessions failed to parse or export". The second case currently renders as "Present in the archive, not reached by this window" — a false statement about a population we DID reach.

Both reduce to the root cause already stated in this ticket: `tally_skips` collapses `list[SkipRecord]` into `dict[SkipReason, int]`, destroying agent identity at aggregation time. Re-keying by `(agent, reason)` unblocks all three symptoms — apportionment, honest cause attribution, and the unreached/skipped distinction.

Both reviews were left OPEN in roborev so the findings stay visible until this lands.

provenance.reason: Deferred roborev findings #95 and #66-F2 into TB-35

data.to:
WHERE: toolbench/report.py:132-181 (`_sampling_notes`, uneven-sampling branch); `tally_skips` at report.py:256; the `--limit` truncation site at passive.py:267-270.

SUPERSEDED SCOPE -- READ FIRST. This ticket was originally built around a blocker that does not exist, and carried two findings that are now fixed. All three claims are struck:

- STRUCK: "`tally_skips` collapses `list[SkipRecord]` into `dict[SkipReason, int]`, destroying agent identity at aggregation time." That is true of `tally_skips`, but irrelevant here -- `_sampling_notes` receives the RAW `list[SkipRecord]` and never calls `tally_skips`. `tally_skips` only feeds the rendered "Skipped by reason" table. The comment now at report.py:102-104 says so explicitly.
- STRUCK: "`SkipRecord` would need to carry the agent, which means the discovery path must stamp it on the ref before the skip is recorded." `SkipRecord` has carried `agent` since TB-23 (sources.py:98-101). Per-agent skip counts need no discovery-path work: `Counter(s.agent for s in skips)` already does it, and shipped at report.py:105.
- STRUCK: the two roborev findings deferred into this ticket by the 2026-07-13 comment -- job #95 (false `--limit` attribution) and job #66 finding 2 (all-skipped agents mislabelled "not reached") -- were FIXED in 24d9c0f. They were never blocked on any re-keying. Both roborev reviews are still OPEN and should be closed against that commit.

WHAT REMAINS: quantitative apportionment. When the spread crosses SPREAD_THRESHOLD and both causes are live, the note (report.py:155-162) can only report that both are live -- "`--limit N` was applied AND 40 sessions were skipped." It cannot say how much of the spread each cause owns, per agent. The sentence it still cannot write is the load-bearing one: "agent X lost 38 of its 40 candidate sessions to attrition, which accounts for the spread; the limit accounts for the rest."

WHY THIS IS STILL REAL WORK. Apportionment needs two numbers per agent, and they cost very different amounts:

(1) The ATTRITION half needs the skip tally re-keyed to `(agent, reason)`. This is cheap and local to the report layer -- the raw records already carry both fields, so it is `Counter((s.agent, s.reason) for s in skips)`, NOT a data-model change. `reason` must stay in the key, because the remedy differs by reason and that is the entire point of apportioning: UNKNOWN_SCHEMA attrition is fixable (write a parser and the spread closes), MISSING_SOURCE attrition is permanent (the transcripts are gone; the spread never closes). "Agent X lost 38 sessions" without the reason cannot tell the reader which of those two worlds they are in.

(2) The TRUNCATION half has NO counter at all, and must not be faked by subtraction. passive.py:267-270 `break`s out of `refs_iter` the moment the limit is hit, so the sessions the limit cut are never enumerated -- nobody counts them. The tempting shortcut is `census.totals[X] - reached(X) - skipped_by_agent[X]`, but that residual is "unaccounted", not "truncated": the report already names other channels that land in the same bucket (a `--since` cutoff, drift between discovery and the census -- see report.py:176-181). Labelling it "limit truncation" would reintroduce the EXACT anti-pattern 24d9c0f removed from this function -- inferring one cause from the absence of the others. Every claim in this note fires on its own signal, and apportionment must hold that line.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION (settle before implementing): where does the truncation count come from?
  (a) RECOMMENDED -- count it at the source. Keep draining `refs_iter` past the limit, counting only (discovery-grain metadata, no exports), so per-agent truncation becomes an OBSERVED number. The only option that gives apportionment a real signal, and the drain is cheap.
  (b) Render the third bucket as "unaccounted" and refuse to name it. Honest and cheaper, but delivers no apportionment -- i.e. abandons this ticket's remaining value.
  (c) Subtract and call it truncation. REJECTED -- see (2).

DONE WHEN: with both causes live, the uneven-sampling note apportions the spread per agent, every number rests on its own observed signal, and the note names no cause it did not measure.

data.body:
**Correction to the 2026-07-13T22:05 scope-widening comment above — it is wrong on every load-bearing point, and this ticket has been rewritten accordingly.**

That comment deferred roborev #95 and #66-F2 into this ticket, asserting both "reduce to the root cause already stated in this ticket: `tally_skips` collapses `list[SkipRecord]` into `dict[SkipReason, int]`, destroying agent identity at aggregation time." They do not, and it does not — not on this path:

- `_sampling_notes` receives the **raw** `list[SkipRecord]`. It never calls `tally_skips`. Agent identity was never destroyed on the way into the note.
- `SkipRecord` has carried `agent` since TB-23 (`sources.py:98-101`). The claimed prerequisite — "the discovery path must stamp it on the ref" — was already satisfied when this ticket was written.

So the blocker was imaginary, and **both deferred findings were fixed directly in `24d9c0f`**, needing no re-keying: `--limit` is now threaded into `_sampling_notes` and each cause is named only when its own signal fires (4-case dispatch, report.py:140-181); zero-session agents are split into `never_looked` vs `all_skipped` off `Counter(s.agent for s in skips)` (report.py:105-130).

**Action:** roborev jobs #95 and #66 were deliberately left OPEN "so the findings stay visible until this lands." They have landed. Both should be closed against `24d9c0f`.

**What this ticket now owns** (title and description rewritten): quantitative apportionment only — splitting a spread across its causes per agent. That is still real work, and it needs `(agent, reason)` re-keying — but the re-keying is cheap and report-local, not the upstream data-model change described above. The genuinely-missing piece is the *truncation* count: `passive.py:267-270` breaks out of `refs_iter` at the limit, so nothing counts what was cut, and deriving it by subtracting reached+skipped from the census total would rebuild the very inference-from-absence bug `24d9c0f` just deleted. See the plan file for the design options.

data.body:
**Design question settled — but NOT with option (a). Option (a) was a bad recommendation and is withdrawn.**

Reading the discovery path invalidates it:

- `_agentsview_pages` (sources.py:238-259) is a `while True` cursor loop, so `limit` is a **page size**, not a hard cap — the refs iterator *would* yield the rest of the archive if drained. But `page_limit = args.limit` (passive.py:250), so the page size equals the limit: draining a 5k-session archive under `--limit 10` costs ~500 `agentsview session list` subprocesses. Option (a) would make `--limit` — a flag whose entire purpose is a cheap run — as expensive as `--all`. Withdrawn.
- It is also unnecessary. Both numbers already exist:
  - `census.totals[X]` — true per-agent archive population, from `_list_total`'s scoped `--limit 1` count read (sources.py:296-310). Not capped by `page_limit`.
  - the refs we actually pulled — `Counter(r.agent for r in refs)`.

**ADOPTED — option (d): `truncated_X = census.totals[X] - sampled_X`, where `sampled_X = Counter(r.agent for r in refs)`.** Both sides are observed. No draining, no new subprocess, no new field on any dataclass.

This is NOT the forbidden subtraction. The one this ticket rejects is `totals[X] - reached(X) - skipped_by_agent[X]`, which routes through the reducer's *session* count: a ref that exports and parses but yields zero calls may produce no reducer session and no `SkipRecord`, so it would be silently attributed to truncation. Counting **refs** avoids the question entirely — a ref was either pulled or it was not.

Two constraints on the implementation:

1. **Count refs AFTER `filter_subagents`** (passive.py:361). The census's `includes` deliberately track the post-filter population (TB-33 Finding 1); counting pre-filter refs against a post-filter denominator recreates exactly the parents-plus-children-over-parents-only bug that finding closed.
2. **Only name truncation when `limit is not None`.** Under `--all` the pages drain to exhaustion, so `totals[X] - sampled_X` should be 0; any nonzero residual there is discovery/census drift, not truncation, and must be reported as such. This keeps the existing discipline: every cause fires on its own signal.

provenance.reason: Withdraw option (a): drain cost is O(archive/limit) subprocesses since page_limit==args.limit. Adopt option (d): totals - sampled_refs, both observed.
